# QuickOper

> Verified-calculation tools for personal money decisions. Every calculation runs
> entirely in the visitor's browser; no input is transmitted, logged or stored.

QuickOper computes, it does not advise. Each tool performs deterministic
arithmetic and publishes its formula, its intermediate values, a full
period-by-period schedule, and the fixture tests proving its output matches a
real published third-party figure.

Nothing on this site is financial, tax or investment advice. The expertise
claimed is computational, not advisory.

## Tools

### Debt payoff calculator — avalanche vs snowball
URL: https://quickoper.com/finance/debt-payoff-calculator
Computes: months to debt freedom and total interest, for the avalanche and
snowball strategies and for a minimum-payments-only baseline, with a full
month-by-month schedule.
Inputs: per-debt balance, annual rate and minimum payment; one total monthly
payment.
Jurisdiction: none. Interest is charged monthly on the opening balance, which
is a convention, not a rule of any one country.
Methodology: https://quickoper.com/methodology
Verification: https://quickoper.com/verify

### Coast FIRE calculator
URL: https://quickoper.com/finance/coast-fire-calculator
Computes: the amount that must already be invested for it to reach a retirement
target with no further contributions, plus a year-by-year projection.
Inputs: current age, retirement age, amount invested, annual spending,
withdrawal rate, real annual return, monthly contribution.
Jurisdiction: none. No tax treatment or account type is modelled.
Methodology: https://quickoper.com/methodology
Verification: https://quickoper.com/verify

## Derivations

### How credit card interest is actually calculated
URL: https://quickoper.com/credit-card-interest
States: a credit card daily periodic rate is APR divided by 365. At 22.99% APR
that is 0.062986% per day. Interest is charged on the average daily balance of
the billing cycle, not the closing balance.
Key figures, all computed on a $6,000 balance at 22.99% APR:
  - 28-day cycle: $105.82. 30-day cycle: $113.38. 31-day cycle: $117.15.
  - APR/12 monthly approximation: $114.95 per month.
  - Over a full year both methods total exactly $1,379.40.
  - With daily compounding, one year costs $1,550.30 - an effective annual
    rate of 25.838% against a stated 22.99%.
  - A $200 payment on a 30-day cycle costs $109.60 of interest if it lands on
    day 1 and $113.25 if it lands on day 30.

### Why a 7% return is not 0.583% a month
URL: https://quickoper.com/monthly-return-rate
States: converting a stated annual RETURN to a monthly rate requires the twelfth
root, not division by twelve. A 7% annual return is 0.565415% per month, being
(1.07)^(1/12) - 1. Dividing gives 0.583333%, which compounds to an effective
7.2290% per year rather than 7%.
Key figures:
  - $100,000 for 30 years at a stated 7%: $761,225.50 using the twelfth root,
    $811,649.75 using r/12. The error overstates by $50,424.24, or 6.62%.
  - The error is always in the flattering direction.
  - An APR is the exception: a lender APR is a nominal rate defined as twelve
    times the monthly rate, so dividing by twelve is correct for debt.
  - Real return is nominal divided by inflation, not minus: 8% nominal against
    3% inflation is (1.08/1.03)-1 = 4.854369%, not 5%. Over 30 years on
    $100,000 that is $414,568.14 against $432,194.24.
